key_insight: EvolveNav turns zero-shot object-goal navigation into a learning-at-test-time problem, so the agent can improve while exploring instead of repeating the same mistakes. It combines proactive preflection with a self-evolving memory to adapt its decisions as it gathers new experience.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of adaptation in zero-shot object-goal navigation. Existing foundation-model-based methods often rely on static priors, which makes them prone to repeated errors, inefficient exploration, and costly trial-and-error behavior.
method: Builds an agentic rule memory that extracts actionable knowledge from navigation experience.
Uses proactive preflection to anticipate likely failures and adjust behavior before making avoidable mistakes.
Continuously updates memory at test time, enabling self-evolving improvement without task-specific training.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical way to improve embodied agents in unseen environments without retraining. It is especially relevant for robotics and navigation systems where online adaptation, efficiency, and robustness matter.

paper_title: EvolveNav: Proactive Preflection and Self-Evolving Memory for Zero-Shot Object Goal Navigation
paper_authors: Qi Chai, Wenhao Shen, Nanjie Yao, Yue Xia, Kaiyong Zhao
